title: Teach the Chore, Then Step Back | Parenting Rewind
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

narration.transcript: A child learning to fold towels will work more slowly and less neatly than an adult who has done it for years. Correcting every corner or taking the towel back can turn a family contribution into a performance test. Pause, demonstrate one manageable step, and leave room for practice. Try: Match these two corners, press the fold once, and place the towel in this stack; I will help if you ask. Clear teaching plus reasonable expectations lets competence grow while the child still contributes real work to the household.
